 Twitch Adds A Version Of Amazon's Shoppable Ads
 by Laurie Sullivan 
 , Staff Writer, 
 Yesterday
 Amazon's live-streaming platform added a shoppable advertising
format last week, announcing it during its creator and fan conference TwitchCon.
 The shoppable ad format rolled out in open beta on Twitch desktop across the U.S. and Canada, turning standard
video ads into an in-stream storefront backed by Amazon's retail checkout.
 Andrea Garabedian, director of Global Go-to-Market for Twitch at Amazon Ads, described
shoppable formats as the link between viewer attention and measurable results, according to one report . advertisement
 advertisement
 “Shoppable ad formats give advertisers a way to meet that intent
instantly, turning the most attentive audience in video into one that can be measured against real business outcomes,” she said.
 Twitch originally launched in 2011 as a spinoff focused
on video games, but it has since grown into a digital hangout for esports, music, cooking, art, and casual conversation
 The shoppable ad format will first roll out in the U.S. and Canada. The
goal appears to be that Amazon wants to turn the service into a full-funnel advertising channel that connects brands with younger, highly engaged audiences.
 Twitch viewers spend more than four
hours a day on the sited on average. Nearly 70% of Twitch’s global audience is Gen Z and millennials, many of whom are not found on other media sites, according to the company.
 About 105
million average monthly visitors come to the Twitch site, and 70% are between the ages of 18 and 24, according to Twitch internal data from 2022 and 2023, respectively.
 The new format appears
as an interactive, clickable overlay on Twitch video ads, shortening the path from brand message to transaction.
 It is built with the same underlying Amazon Ads technology and checkout system
as Prime Video's interactive ads, allowing viewers to browse different styles and add items directly to their Amazon cart without leaving the stream, Twitch's placement is tailored to a different
viewing environment.
 Unlike Prime Video's living-room TV focus, Twitch’s shoppable ads are available today only on desktop, with plans for mobile and connected TV in the future.
 For marketers, the setup is streamlined. They can toggle the feature on within existing Twitch video campaigns or purchase the inventory alongside Prime Video via the Amazon Ads Agent.
 The
platform in December also will roll out a skippable ad in open beta.
